action_items.item: Add tests that run the account-page spend summary with legacy-checkout-fallback both on and off, including the zero-denominator case. Run them in CI.
Require flag changes on io-shop to roll out gradually, or to be checked against error rate before reaching all traffic. Roll back automatically if errors rise.
Alert on a rise in the account-page error rate shortly after a flag change, and show recent flag changes in the alert.

causal_chain.step: Users saw account-page requests fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average, peaking at {errors_at_worst}, and the HighErrorRate alert fired.
The failing requests raised a ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
Account-page traffic began taking the code path that contains that line when the flag legacy-checkout-fallback went from mostly on to mostly off at 07:12. The errors began at the same minute.
The flag was switched off with no deploy or release in the window. The flag change was the only change found, so the flag flip is what exposed the latent bug in the non-fallback path.
Putting the flag back on (M1) stopped the errors and the metrics returned to baseline. This confirms the flag state as the trigger.

contributing_factors.factor: The code path at spend_summary.py:47 divides without guarding against zero. It was reachable only when the flag was off, so the bug stayed hidden until the flag changed.
Nothing checked that the flag-off path works before the flag was flipped. A flag change in production can reach untested code and go to all traffic at once.
The alert fired about five minutes after onset. Nothing linked the rise in errors to the flag change.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, a large share of account-page requests on the shop failed. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. A feature flag was switched off. That exposed a code path with a division-by-zero bug. No deploy or release happened in the period. Argus switched the flag back on, and the error rate returned to baseline. A draft pull request with a code fix was opened for review. Argus held the incident for {held}, which measures the response and not the outage.

got_lucky: The failing path hit only part of the traffic and the flag could be reverted at once. A change that needed a deploy to undo would have lasted longer.
went_well: Argus found the flag change and reverted it within seconds of the alert being received.
The revert was checked against the metrics before the incident was marked mitigated.
A draft fix was proposed straight away.
went_wrong: The flag was changed without anyone knowing the off path was broken.
The alert fired several minutes after the errors began.

input.root_cause: The feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at about 07:12Z. That sent account-page requests down a path in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py (line 47) that raises a ZeroDivisionError. The path was only safe while the flag was on.
